quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: She's very modest, ___ her brother, who never stops boasting about his achievements.
quests.completeSentence: She's very modest, unlike her brother, who never stops boasting about his achievements.
quests.contextClue: The two siblings are contrasted.
quests.hint: A preposition that shows two people are different.
quests.explanation: 'Unlike' + noun compares by contrast: 'Unlike her brother, she is modest.' Its opposite 'like' shows similarity.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'unlike' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'unlike' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: The match will go ahead ___ of the weather, so bring waterproofs just in case.
quests.completeSentence: The match will go ahead regardless of the weather, so bring waterproofs just in case.
quests.contextClue: The plan does not change with the weather, yet waterproofs are advised.
quests.hint: It means 'without being affected by'.
quests.explanation: 'Regardless of' + noun means despite; the conditions don't matter: 'regardless of the weather'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'regardless' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'regardless' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: You have to finish the project on time, ___ it takes, even if that means working weekends.
quests.completeSentence: You have to finish the project on time, whatever it takes, even if that means working weekends.
quests.contextClue: Working weekends is an example of the effort.
quests.hint: A word that leaves the amount of effort open.
quests.explanation: 'Whatever it takes' means do everything necessary. 'Whatever' can also mean 'anything that': 'Do whatever you like'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'whatever' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'whatever' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Call me ___ you need help, day or night; I'm a light sleeper.

quests.contextClue: 'Day or night' means any moment.
quests.hint: At any time that.
quests.explanation: 'Whenever' means every time or at any time that. It is written as one word.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'whenever' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'whenever' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I'll follow you ___ you go, as long as we stay together.

quests.contextClue: Staying together matters more than the place.
quests.hint: In any place that.
quests.explanation: 'Wherever' means in any place that: 'wherever you go'. It is written as one word.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'wherever' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'wherever' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Only one thing matters in this negotiation, ___ trust; without it, nothing else works.
quests.completeSentence: Only one thing matters in this negotiation, namely trust; without it, nothing else works.
quests.contextClue: The general 'one thing' is then named.
quests.hint: A word that introduces the specific item you have just referred to.
quests.explanation: 'Namely' introduces the specific detail you are about to name: 'one thing matters, namely trust'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'namely' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'namely' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Moving abroad will be difficult, but in the end I think the benefits will ___ the drawbacks.

quests.hint: Be greater in importance than something else.
quests.explanation: 'Outweigh' means be more important than: 'the benefits outweigh the risks'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'outweigh' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'outweigh' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: With the company expanding so fast, a few mistakes were ___.

quests.contextClue: Fast expansion leads to errors that cannot be avoided.
quests.hint: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
quests.explanation: 'Inevitable' means certain to happen. The adverb is 'inevitably'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'inevitable' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'inevitable' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: I ___ on paying for dinner tonight; you paid last time, and I won't take no for an answer.

quests.contextClue: 'Won't take no for an answer' shows firmness.
quests.hint: Demand firmly that something happens.
quests.explanation: 'Insist on' + -ing or noun means firmly demand: 'insist on paying'. It is used to refuse a polite protest.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'insist' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'insist' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: It's easy to ___ small details when you are rushing to meet a deadline.
quests.completeSentence: It's easy to overlook small details when you are rushing to meet a deadline.
quests.contextClue: Rushing reduces attention to detail.
quests.hint: Fail to notice or consider.
quests.explanation: 'Overlook' means fail to see or consider something: 'overlook a detail'. It can also mean have a view over: 'overlooks the sea'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'overlook' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'overlook' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Never ___ how long a simple repair can take once you actually start.
quests.completeSentence: Never underestimate how long a simple repair can take once you actually start.
quests.contextClue: 'How long... once you start' warns against optimism.
quests.hint: Think something is smaller or easier than it really is.
quests.explanation: 'Underestimate' means judge something to be less than it is. The opposite is 'overestimate'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'underestimate' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'underestimate' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: It took hours to ___ her that the plan was safe, but she finally agreed.
quests.completeSentence: It took hours to convince her that the plan was safe, but she finally agreed.
quests.contextClue: Belief in safety is the goal.
quests.hint: Make someone believe something is true.
quests.explanation: 'Convince someone that...' means make them believe. 'Persuade someone to...' is about getting them to act.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'convince' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'convince' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: She began to ___ her brother because he always got the credit for work they did together.
quests.completeSentence: She began to resent her brother because he always got the credit for work they did together.
quests.contextClue: Unequal credit explains the feeling.
quests.hint: Feel bitter about something unfair.
quests.explanation: 'Resent' means feel angry or bitter about something you think is unfair. It can be followed by a noun or -ing.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'resent' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'resent' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: The new tax is highly ___; some people love it, and others hate it.

quests.contextClue: Love and hate show a divided opinion.
quests.hint: Causing strong disagreement.
quests.explanation: 'Controversial' describes topics that people argue about. The noun is 'controversy'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'controversial' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'controversial' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.textWithBlank: The advertisement was ___: it promised free delivery, but customers were charged for shipping.

quests.hint: Giving a false impression.
quests.explanation: 'Misleading' describes information that gives a false impression, though it may not be an outright lie. The verb is 'mislead'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'misleading' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'misleading' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.textWithBlank: Meeting her at the airport was pure ___; neither of us knew the other was travelling.

quests.contextClue: Neither person planned it.
quests.hint: Two events happening together by chance.
quests.explanation: A 'coincidence' is two things happening at the same time by chance. The adjective is 'coincidental'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'coincidence' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'coincidence' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Elderly people who live alone can be especially ___ to scams.

quests.explanation: 'Vulnerable to' + noun means easily harmed by something: 'vulnerable to infection'.

quests.hint: An adverb that shows doubt about what people say.

quests.articulationTip: Connect 'supposedly' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.textWithBlank: She ___ agreed to help, although she had plenty of her own work to finish.

quests.contextClue: Her own workload explains her unwillingness.
quests.hint: An adverb meaning without wanting to.
quests.explanation: 'Reluctantly' means unwillingly. The adjective is 'reluctant': 'reluctant to help'.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'reluctantly' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'reluctantly' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.

quests.contextClue: 'But within a year' contrasts with the start.
quests.hint: At the beginning.
quests.explanation: 'Initially' means at the start. It often appears before a contrast with what happened later.
quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'initially' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.
quests.articulationTip: Connect 'initially' smoothly with the surrounding words to maintain natural spoken tempo.

quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'cope' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.

quests.phoneticGuide: Articulate 'reimburse' clearly with accurate syllable stress and steady oral projection.

quests.instruction: Study the context clue, discover the missing word, and practice oral articulation.
quests.textWithBlank: Neither side got everything it wanted, so the final deal was a ___.
quests.completeSentence: Neither side got everything it wanted, so the final deal was a compromise.
quests.contextClue: Both sides were only partly satisfied.
quests.hint: An agreement where each side gives something up.
quests.explanation: A 'compromise' is an agreement in which both sides make concessions. It is also a verb: 'compromise on price'.
